The speaker has owned Amazon for over 20 years, noting it compounded well, and cites it as a great business example for real options.
The speaker references Costco as an example of a great business that one should latch onto and hold if convinced.

thesis: This episode argues for an 'expectations investing' approach, using long-term holdings like Berkshire Hathaway, Amazon, and Costco as examples of businesses that have compounded well over decades. It suggests investors should identify great businesses with characteristics similar to early Amazon and hold them if convinced, citing Shopify as a modern case study.
